paper.title: Discovery of a Makemakean Moon
paper.assessment: Complete six-page author manuscript retained; sections 2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.2, 3.3 and Table1 assessed; figure captions read, no figure embedded. Final publisher record and later orbit/thermal updates not audited.
paper.terms: Specific record nonexclusive distribution; not CC BY, no blanket image/data/paper licence assertion.

observations.association: Publisher 4350 seconds equals six 725-second exposures for one visit; the April27/29 metadata covers two visits, not proof the native JPEG combines both. Moon detected in all six visit1 long exposures, not recovered in visit2; exact publisher JPEG/raw-product crosswalk remains open.
observations.processing: Median co-registered visit2 subtraction for five visit1 photometry frames; sixth excluded for nearby cosmic ray. Saturated primary in long frames; four short exposures stacked for primary brightness. Detection/nondetection and glare mask constrain visibility, not absence of a moon.

measured.notes: Reported paper measurements/estimates retained, no independent angular/raster calculation; not a calibration of the publisher JPEG or local chemistry/colour.

assumptionsAndModels.Vband: F350LP delta adopted for V without moon colour information; H_V7.89±0.04 inferred using primary H_V0.091±0.015. Not measured moon visible colour.
assumptionsAndModels.orbit: Preliminary prograde circular pass/fail models with assumed primary density1.4–3.2g/cm3 permit a21100–300000km and period12.4–660days; retrograde mirrors also acceptable. Discovery data alone do not constrain primary density or measure system mass. These historical conditional ranges are not current ephemerides, uncertainty posteriors, spin periods or permanent-facing-site evidence.
assumptionsAndModels.size: Nominal geometric albedo0.04 implies diameter175km; albedo0.02 implies about250km. No resolved axes, measured local albedo or silent catalogue size update. NASA100-mile caption estimate remains distinct.
assumptionsAndModels.thermal: Dark-moon hypothesis reallocates some system thermal excess from primary to moon. NEATM alternatives use albedo0.04/eta0.25,0.02/eta0.4,or0.04/eta0.4 with H brighter by0.5mag; models produce60–80percent of measured24micron system flux, not a unique complete solution. Not observed local dark patches, chemistry, fractions, calibrated visible colour or terrain.
assumptionsAndModels.origin: Capture, giant impact and atmospheric-interaction explanations are hypotheses, not directly measured history. Primary pole/flattening/thermal-inertia discussion is conditional and must not be assigned as moon measurements.
